intro: People all over the world mark a space before a match. In Brazil, people stand in a circle. In England, boxers moved into a square with ropes. Fencers meet on a long, thin strip.
In this unit, you will meet these rooms. You will learn their names in many languages. You will hear how music can start a room. You will learn some laws and dates too.
By the end, you can name a room by its shape. You can tell where it comes from. You can tell one thing that happened to it in history.
bigQuestion: How does a shape on the floor, or a song, make a room for a match?

title: The Circle on the Floor

chapters.title: Circle, Square, Strip
chapters.bigQuestion: How does the shape on the floor tell people where a match can happen?

story.title: Tape on the Gym Floor
story.kicker: A line of tape turns a plain floor into a place with rules.
paragraphs: It is morning in a school gym. The floor is wide and empty. A teacher kneels down with a roll of white tape. She presses it to the floor, bit by bit.
Slowly the tape bends into a big circle. Now the floor has an inside and an outside. Nobody has stepped in yet. But everyone can see where the circle is.
People have marked floors like this for a very long time. In Japan, sumo wrestlers meet inside a round ring called a dohyo. In Brazil, people stand in a circle called a roda.
A shape on the floor is a rule you can see. It says where the match happens. It says where people watch. The tape tells everyone before a single word is said.
story.think: What shapes have you seen marked on a floor or a field?

lessons.title: The Roda in Brazil
lessons.mainIdea: In capoeira, people make a circle called the roda.
reading: *Capoeira* comes from Brazil. Africans and their children in Brazil made it. They lived under slavery there. Capoeira mixes game, music and movement.
Capoeira happens in a *roda*. Roda means wheel or circle in Portuguese. People stand around the edge. Two players go into the middle at a time.

words.d: an Afro-Brazilian art that mixes game, music and movement
the circle of people where capoeira happens; the word means wheel in Portuguese

look.title: Picture the Roda
look.text: Look at a ring of people standing close together. Some hold music makers. Some clap. The middle of the ring is empty. It waits for two players.
look.prompt: Where is the inside of this room, and where is the outside?

check.q: What is a roda?
check.why: In capoeira, the roda is the circle of people. The word means wheel.

check.q: Where does capoeira come from?
check.why: Capoeira is Afro-Brazilian. It grew in Brazil.

check.q: Who made capoeira?
choices: Africans and their children in Brazil
check.why: Capoeira grew among Africans and their children in Brazil.

lessons.title: The Sumo Ring
lessons.mainIdea: Sumo wrestlers meet inside a round ring called a dohyo.
reading: *Sumo* is a very old sport from Japan. The wrestlers meet on a raised platform. It is made of packed clay. On top is a round ring called a *dohyo*.
The ring is marked with straw bales. It is about 15 feet across. A wrestler loses if he steps out of the ring. So the circle is a rule you can see.

words.d: an old style of wrestling from Japan
the round ring where sumo wrestlers meet

look.title: Straw on the Clay
look.text: Look at a high square of hard clay. On top, a ring of straw bales makes a circle. Sand is swept smooth all around it. The ring is empty and still.
look.prompt: Why might the ring be marked with straw you can see?

check.q: What is a dohyo?
check.why: The dohyo is the round ring where sumo wrestlers meet.

check.q: What happens if a sumo wrestler steps out of the ring?
check.why: In sumo, stepping out of the ring loses the match.

check.q: Where does sumo come from?
check.why: Sumo is a very old sport from Japan.

lessons.title: Ropes Around a Square
lessons.mainIdea: A boxing ring is a square, even though it is called a ring.
reading: Long ago in England, boxers fought inside a circle of people. That circle was called a *ring*. Later, rules asked for posts and ropes.
The shape became a square. But the old name stayed. Today a boxing ring is a square with *ropes* on four sides. Posts stand at the four corners.

words.d: the place where a match happens; a boxing ring is a square
the lines of rope that close in the four sides of a boxing ring

look.title: Four Corners
look.text: Look at a raised square floor. Three ropes run around its sides. A post stands in each corner. People sit in chairs all around it.
look.prompt: Why is it strange to call this square a ring?

check.q: What shape is a boxing ring today?
check.why: A boxing ring is a square with ropes, though its name is ring.

check.q: Why is it called a ring?
choices: Long ago, people stood in a circle around boxers.
check.why: In old England, a circle of people made the ring. The name stayed.

check.q: What stands at the four corners of a boxing ring?
check.why: A boxing ring has a post in each corner, with ropes between them.

lessons.title: A Rule Book Names the Ring
lessons.mainIdea: In 1867, the Queensberry Rules said how big a boxing ring should be.
reading: In 1867, a set of boxing *rules* came out in England. They are called the Queensberry Rules. They carry the name of the Marquess of Queensberry.
The first rule was about the room. It asked for a ring 24 feet across. The rules also asked boxers to wear gloves. Boxing still uses gloves today.

words.d: written directions everyone in a sport agrees to follow

look.title: The First Queensberry Rule
look.text: The match should be in a ring 24 feet across, or as close to that size as the place allows.
look.prompt: What did this rule tell people to set up first?

check.q: When did the Queensberry Rules come out?
check.why: The Queensberry Rules came out in England in 1867.

check.q: How big a ring did the first rule ask for?
check.why: Rule 1 asked for a ring 24 feet across.

check.q: What else did the Queensberry Rules ask boxers to wear?
check.why: The Queensberry Rules asked boxers to wear gloves.

lessons.title: The Fencing Strip
lessons.mainIdea: Fencers meet on a long, thin strip called a piste.
reading: *Fencing* is a sport with long, thin swords. The tips are blunt. Fencers wear masks and white jackets. Fencing was in the first modern Olympics in 1896.
Fencers meet on a long, thin *piste*. Piste is a French word. The strip is 14 meters long. It is only about 2 meters wide. Fencers stay on the strip.

words.d: a sport with long, thin swords with blunt tips
the long, thin strip where fencers meet

look.title: A Long Line
look.text: Look at a long, narrow strip on the floor. It is much longer than it is wide. Lines cross it near the middle and near each end. Two people in white masks stand on it.
look.prompt: How is this strip different from a circle?

check.q: What is a piste?
check.why: The piste is the long, thin strip where fencers meet.

check.q: How long is a fencing strip?
check.why: The strip is 14 meters long and about 2 meters wide.

check.q: When was fencing first in the modern Olympics?
check.why: Fencing was in the first modern Olympics in 1896.

lessons.title: Mats for Judo and Wrestling
lessons.mainIdea: Judo and wrestling happen on soft mats with lines that mark the space.
reading: *Judo* began in Japan in 1882. Its rooms used soft floor mats called *tatami*. Today judo mats are square. Judo joined the Olympics in 1964 in Tokyo.
Olympic wrestling uses a round shape on a square mat. The circle is 9 meters across. So some rooms mix shapes. A circle can sit on a square.

words.d: a martial art and sport that began in Japan in 1882
soft, thick floor mats used in Japanese rooms

check.why: Judo began in Japan in 1882. It joined the Olympics in 1964.

check.why: Tatami are soft, thick floor mats used in Japanese rooms.

check.q: What shape is marked on an Olympic wrestling mat?
check.why: Olympic wrestling uses a circle 9 meters across on a square mat.

review.why: The roda is a circle of people.

review.q: Which room is a square with ropes?
review.why: A boxing ring is a square with ropes on four sides.
Fencers meet on a long strip called a piste.

review.q: Which sport uses a ring called a dohyo?
review.why: Sumo wrestlers meet in the dohyo.

chapters.title: A Song in a Circle
chapters.bigQuestion: How can music tell people that a room has begun?

story.title: The Bow by the Wall
story.kicker: A tall bow with one string waits for its turn.
paragraphs: A tall wooden bow leans against a wall. It has one metal string. A round, dry gourd is tied near the bottom. It is not for arrows. It is a music maker called a berimbau.
In the room, people stand in a circle. They are waiting. The middle of the circle is empty. Nobody goes in yet. Everyone looks at the bow by the wall.
A teacher picks up the berimbau. She taps the string with a thin stick. A low sound rings out. A drum joins in. Then a small hand drum with jingles joins too.
Now the room has begun. In many capoeira schools, the music opens the roda. The song tells people it is time. The circle is ready.
story.think: What sound tells you that something at school is starting?

lessons.title: The Berimbau
lessons.mainIdea: The berimbau is a bow with one string that leads capoeira music.
reading: The *berimbau* is a music maker from Brazil. It is a wooden bow with one metal string. A dry gourd is tied to it. The gourd makes the sound louder.
Bows like this were played in parts of Africa too. People brought this music with them to Brazil. In many capoeira rodas, the berimbau leads all the music.

words.d: a wooden bow with one metal string and a gourd, used in capoeira music

look.title: Look at the Bow
look.text: Look at a long, bent stick of wood. One wire runs from end to end. Near the bottom hangs a round gourd, open on one side. A thin stick and a small stone rest beside it.
look.prompt: Which part do you think helps make the sound louder?

check.q: What is a berimbau?
check.why: The berimbau is a wooden bow with one metal string.

check.q: What does the gourd on a berimbau do?
check.why: The dry gourd makes the sound of the string louder.

check.q: Where else were bows like this played?
check.why: Musical bows were played in parts of Africa, and people brought them to Brazil.

lessons.title: Drums and Clapping
lessons.mainIdea: Drums, a hand drum and clapping join the berimbau in the roda.
reading: The berimbau does not play alone. A tall drum called the *atabaque* often joins. It stands on the floor. A player hits the top with bare hands.
A *pandeiro* often joins too. It is a small hand drum with jingles. People in the circle clap along. Together they make the sound of the roda.

words.d: a tall drum played with the hands in capoeira
a small hand drum with jingles, like a tambourine

look.title: Music Makers in One Roda
look.unit: instruments in a Capoeira Angola group

look.prompt: Which music maker is there most?

check.q: What is an atabaque?
check.why: The atabaque is a tall drum played with the hands.

check.q: What is a pandeiro?
check.why: The pandeiro is a small hand drum with jingles.

check.q: What do people in the circle often do?
check.why: People in the roda clap along with the music.

lessons.title: One Voice, Then Many
lessons.mainIdea: In capoeira songs, one person sings and the circle answers.
reading: Capoeira songs are sung in *Portuguese*. That is the main language of Brazil. Many songs tell about places, people and history.
Often one person sings a line. Then the whole circle sings back. This is called *call and response*. It is common in music from Africa and Brazil.

words.d: the main language spoken in Brazil
a way of singing where one person sings and a group answers

look.title: Who Sings Next?
look.text: Picture a circle of people. One person sings a short line alone. Then everyone sings the same answer together. Then the one voice sings again.
look.prompt: How does this way of singing bring the whole circle in?

check.q: What language are capoeira songs sung in?
check.why: Capoeira songs are sung in Portuguese, the main language of Brazil.

check.q: What is call and response?
choices: One sings, and the group answers.
check.why: In call and response, one person sings and the group sings back.

check.q: What do many capoeira songs tell about?
check.why: Many capoeira songs tell about places, people and history.

lessons.title: Music in Muay Thai
lessons.mainIdea: In Thailand, Muay Thai matches often have live music.
reading: *Muay Thai* is a combat sport from Thailand. It is also its national sport. Many matches there have live music. A small band plays near the ring.
Before a match, fighters often honor their teachers. This is called the *wai khru*. Music plays during it. A wind pipe and drums make the sound.

words.d: a combat sport from Thailand
a way Muay Thai fighters honor their teachers before a match

look.title: Two Rooms With Music
look.text: In a capoeira roda, the berimbau leads. People stand in a circle. In a Muay Thai match in Thailand, a band sits by a square ring. A wind pipe and drums play.
look.prompt: How are these two rooms alike, and how are they different?

check.q: Where does Muay Thai come from?
check.why: Muay Thai comes from Thailand.

check.q: What is the wai khru?
check.why: In the wai khru, Muay Thai fighters honor their teachers before a match.

check.q: What plays music at many Muay Thai matches in Thailand?
check.why: A small band with a wind pipe and drums plays near the ring.

lessons.title: Once Against the Law
lessons.mainIdea: Brazil once made capoeira against the law, then later let it be taught.
reading: Brazil ended *slavery* in 1888. Two years later, in 1890, a new law made capoeira a crime. People could be jailed for it.
Teachers kept capoeira alive. In the 1930s, Mestre Bimba opened a school in Salvador, Bahia. Capoeira was taught in the open. *Mestre* means master teacher.

words.d: when people are owned and forced to work without pay or freedom
a master teacher of capoeira; the word is Portuguese

look.title: Two Laws, Two Years
look.text: In 1888, a law in Brazil ended slavery. In 1890, a new law made capoeira a crime. Many people who played capoeira were Black Brazilians.
look.prompt: Why do you think the second law was unfair to Black Brazilians?

check.q: When did Brazil end slavery?
check.why: Brazil ended slavery in 1888.

check.q: What did the 1890 law do?
check.why: In 1890, a law in Brazil made capoeira a crime.

check.q: What does mestre mean?
check.why: Mestre is Portuguese for a master teacher.

lessons.title: Honored by the World
lessons.mainIdea: In 2014, UNESCO honored the capoeira circle.
reading: *UNESCO* is a group from the United Nations. It honors culture from around the world. It keeps lists of songs, crafts and ways of life.
In 2014, UNESCO added the capoeira circle to one of these lists. The list is for living *heritage*. That means culture people still share today.

words.d: a United Nations group that honors culture and learning
ways of life, songs and crafts passed down to new people

look.cite: Lei Aurea, Brazil, 1888; Penal Code of Brazil, 1890; UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list, 2014

check.why: Heritage means ways of life, songs and crafts passed down.

choices: It honors culture from around the world.
check.why: UNESCO is a United Nations group that honors culture.
